title: Trace–diagonal datum
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type between the finite-type $k$-schemes of those conventions; put
$W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ and
diagonal $\Delta$, and let $L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be
tensor-invertible, meaning that there are an object $L^{-1}$ and an isomorphism $L\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}L^{-1}\cong\Lambda_X$. A *trace–diagonal datum* for $(f,L)$ is a
pair

$$
\operatorname{tr}_f:Rf_!L\longrightarrow\Lambda_Y,
\qquad
\operatorname{cl}_\Delta:\Delta_!\Lambda_X\longrightarrow p_2^*L.
$$

Use the fibre product of [def-pc-fibre-product]; the diagonal is the unique map with $p_1\Delta=p_2\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$. All unmarked pullbacks in the displayed formulas are derived pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and $\Delta_!$ means $R\Delta_!$ of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. As required by [def-pur-conventions], the construction is made directly for $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$; its higher-coefficient versions mean the separately specified transports in the purity chapter.

The *induced functor* is

$$
G_L:D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda),
\qquad G_L(K)=Lf^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}L,
$$

and $\operatorname{tr}_f$ defines, via the projection formula, the
*counit*

$$
\epsilon_K:Rf_!G_L(K)\cong K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Y}Rf_!L
\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{id}\otimes\operatorname{tr}_f\ }K;
$$

$\operatorname{cl}_\Delta$ defines the *unit*

$$
\eta_A:A\cong Rp_{2!}\bigl(p_1^*A\otimes^L_{\Lambda_W}\Delta_!\Lambda_X\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{id}\otimes\operatorname{cl}_\Delta\ }
Rp_{2!}\bigl(p_1^*A\otimes^L_{\Lambda_W}p_2^*L\bigr)
\cong G_L(Rf_!A).
$$

The two *triangular composites* are the composites

$$
Rf_!A\xrightarrow{\ Rf_!\eta_A\ }Rf_!G_LRf_!A
\xrightarrow{\ \epsilon_{Rf_!A}\ }Rf_!A
$$

and

$$
G_LK\xrightarrow{\ \eta_{G_LK}\ }G_LRf_!G_LK
\xrightarrow{\ G_L\epsilon_K\ }G_LK,
$$

natural in $A\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$.

The formulas specify composites of the following canonical maps, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms of their values. The compact-support projection is the transformation of [def-exchange-projection], inverted on the finite-Tor domain by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. The needed finite-Tor etale origins are supplied by [lem-sfb-constructible-local-tor-etale-origin]: the global Tor interval of an object of $D^b_{ctf}$ gives the local Tor condition of that lemma by [lem-sfb-proetale-tor-local-global], and its constructible cohomology sheaves are affine-locally constructible by restricting their finite constructible stratification to each affine open. Tensor symmetry is the signed derived symmetry of [lem-pur-derived-tensor-additive-constraints]; the unit constraint is induced by multiplication $P\otimes_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda_X\to P$ on a K-flat representative. The first isomorphism in the unit is the inverse of
$$
 Rp_{2!}(Lp_1^*A\otimes^L R\Delta_!\Lambda_X)
 \cong Rp_{2!}R\Delta_!(L\Delta^*Lp_1^*A)
 \cong A.
$$
Here the first arrow is projection for $\Delta$, the pullback comparison uses [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition, lem-pur-proetale-constant-ring-composition, lem-pur-proetale-derived-pullback-identity] and $p_1\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$, and the second uses compact-support composition [thm-sf-comp-composition] and $p_2\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$. At the identity, use the trivial compactification $(\operatorname{id},\operatorname{id})$, whose functor is the identity. The final isomorphism in the unit is
$$
 Rp_{2!}(Lp_1^*A\otimes^L Lp_2^*L)
 \cong (Rp_{2!}Lp_1^*A)\otimes^L L
 \cong Lf^*Rf_!A\otimes^L L,
$$
using inverse projection for $p_2$ and the inverse of the canonical compact-support exchange for the Cartesian self-square of $f$ [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. In the middle arrow defining $\eta_A$, $Rp_{2!}$ is applied to $1_{Lp_1^*A}\otimes\operatorname{cl}_\Delta$. No triangular identity is part of the datum: the two displayed composites are simply natural endomorphisms.

proof.text: For twisted_preserves, use the completed source-library theorem constructibleFiniteTor_leftDerivedFunctor_upperStar_obj to preserve the native finite-Tor constructible property under pullback. For tensor closure, extract bounded constructible etale origins of both factors from the definition of that property. Reflect their Tor intervals with torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_iff, apply the native etale constructibleFiniteTor_tensor theorem, and transport the result through the monoidal comparison and the two origin isomorphisms. Tensor and pullback functoriality give the displayed action of G_L on morphisms. This avoids the intrinsic constant-ring pullback and tensor wrappers.

proof.text: For shriek_preserves, the fixed finite coefficient quotient has a positive invertible annihilating exponent, supplied by finiteComparedInvertibleExponent. Apply constructibleFiniteTor_rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification to the chosen Nagata compactification. For diagonal_inputs, transport the etale tensor unit through the canonical comparison unit isomorphism, and apply native pullback preservation to p1.

source.place: Functoriality and the canonical component formulas of def-pur-td-datum.md; native finite-coefficient realization

proof.text: Use the canonical maps of def-pur-finite-trace-canonical-maps (projectionCore, contractionCore, exchangeCore, signedSymmetry, unitRight), from which the unit and counit are composed. For counit naturality compose the proved native projection naturality square, signed symmetry, tensor naturality for the fixed trace, and right unit naturality. For unit naturality use lem-pur-finite-diagonal-contraction-naturality and invert its square, use tensor naturality for the fixed diagonal class, then lem-pur-finite-diagonal-exchange-naturality. Apply Rp2! to the tensor square and compose all three equalities by associativity. This is a genuine reduction: neither lower statement contains the datum trace or diagonal class, nor the complete unit composite. The generic canonical data has been extracted verbatim into its own definition module, avoiding an import cycle.

There are no new nodes. The blueprint pair, G_L, ε, η and both triangular composites are kept verbatim. The additions (finite-type k-schemes; the explicit meaning of tensor-invertible; the finite-stage Λ=A_{E,n} with higher-coefficient transports, copied from def-pur-conventions; the canonical-map paragraph) do not weaken the definition. Map checks: (1) The counit is PF_f with the ctf object K pulled back, as lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula requires, plus signed symmetry σ. (2) The first unit iso is PF_Δ with Lp_1^*A in D^b_ctf(W) by pullback-tor-amplitude, LΔ^*Lp_1^*≅id by the three pullback lemmas, and Rp_{2!}RΔ_!≅R(id)_!=id by thm-sf-comp-composition. (3) The last unit iso is PF_{p_2} and then the inverse of the thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale exchange for X'=W, g'=p_1, f'=p_2, g=f; its direction f^{-1}Rf_!→Rp_{2!}p_1^{-1} is correct and Y is qcqs. (4) Both composites are typed in ctf by lem-sf-native-finite-tor-preservation(i). Step 1 (pullback-tor-amplitude, tensor-ctf(ii), tensor functoriality) is correct. Edge cases checked: f=id, X empty, tr=0 or cl=0, L=Λ_X. No cycle (closure 13612 nodes).
